continued_diagnostic_semantics_static_re.assessment: Only three protocol-pinned entry/phase96/phase104 paths/hashes are accepted. Complete tag/progress/counters and semantic identity checks precede strict model state loading. weights_only=True and narrow NumPy safe globals are used. No optimizer/RNG/episode restoration, eligibility transition or checkpoint writer is called. Real checkpoint contents were not deserialized in this review.

Both controls compare all nine fields after validating and indexing all 64 unique seeds and episode-index mapping. Completion order is immaterial. Exact entry and phase96 matches gate every sampled evaluation. No extra control evaluation is added.

64 fresh independent B1 D2 environments, sorted shrinking active batches, MPS float32 model inference, K4 and 18000 cap are preserved. No reset/filler path exists. Each sample evaluation seeds Torch and MPS once after model loading, then uses a batched Categorical draw with controller seeds 64001/64002/64003. No CPU inference fallback exists.

Fixed order is 12 evaluations of 64 episodes, totaling 768. Inference uses model.eval and torch.no_grad; gradients are checked. No optimizer construction, update, student, B/E evaluation or checkpoint-write path is present in the helper. This is source evidence, not measured counters from a campaign.

Three sampled replicates are averaged within each of 64 game seeds before paired differences. 10000 shared-index bootstrap resamples use seed 764002 and percentile 95% intervals. Both 100-alive-frame/1-score margins must support similarity or an advantage; otherwise mixed/inconclusive. phase104 remains primary; no checkpoint selection or automatic training follows.

Decision probabilities/actions/entropy/margins are streamed. Observation presence and first observed K4 decision-boundary visibility are context only. Death cause stays UNKNOWN; no killer or collision attribution is inferred.

One start_new_session worker is owned by the supervisor. Cleanup targets only its recorded new-session group, reaps the leader and separately records cleanup duration. EPERM absence proof uses the process table; absence/probe uncertainty prevents stable hashing. Guard failures remain latched and copied into failed status. Real process-group cleanup and RSS/MPS behavior were not executed by this review.

findings.consequence: A canceled diagnostic can exit 0 with run-result.json and authoritative finalization-result.json both complete and a valid artifact manifest. The original brief requires cancellation to fail the entire run. This finding concerns terminal status; the probe does not establish any inference after cancellation.
findings.finding: defer() sets the cancellation handler flag before all cleanup and normal finalization. The handler ignores signals once that flag is true and does not record a new cancellation request. After cleanup, the same deferred handler remains installed through guard.close(), verify(), receipt/counter collection and stream closure. A signal in that interval leaves result.status complete. publish_terminal then installs a fresh handler, without learning that cancellation was already requested, and publishes successful terminal evidence.
findings.provenance: The defer pattern predates r2. This is a newly identified remaining issue in the reviewed r2 supervisor, not a claim that the repair introduced it.
findings.required_resolution: Keep owned-group cleanup protected from interruption, but separately latch every cancellation request. Before publishing success, fail the result when cancellation arrived during cleanup or final verification. Add a regression that invokes the installed SIGINT/SIGTERM handler during successful supervisor cleanup/guard closure/final verification and requires exit 1, partial status, and no success terminal receipt.
findings.retained_test_gap: test_finalization.py:54-63 mocks guard.close as a clock advance only. Its cancellation-free fixtures do not cover a signal while supervise has called defer(). The new publish_terminal cancellation handler itself fails closed in the independent probes.

synthetic_evidence.method: Actual frozen supervise and publish_terminal; fake completed worker/clock/guard and an in-memory filesystem. Guard.close invokes signal.getsignal(SIGTERM)(SIGTERM, None). No OS signal was sent, no worker subprocess was created, and no filesystem fixture was written.

findings.title: Deferred cancellation during final cleanup/verification can still produce complete
findings.trigger: The worker has completed successfully before the deadline, then SIGINT or SIGTERM arrives after supervise enters its finally block and before the outer cancellation_signals context exits. Guard shutdown and final input verification are concrete points in this window.

independent_synthetic_review.probe_adapter_correction: The first in-memory filesystem adapter lacked Path passthrough and raised TypeError before completing a probe. It wrote no fixture files and is not evidence of a product defect. The corrected adapter completed all six supervisor cases and 15 asserted publication cases.

retained_test_evidence.assessment: Negative controls discriminate the reported late-finalization and unstable-group defects using actual supervisor calls. They are not merely import/API failures. Positive fixtures verify terminal/manifest consistency and one-shot publication errors. Their fake guard/worker/clock do not prove real cleanup, resource cadence, inference semantics or 600-second feasibility. The 44-case suite imports Torch, so it was inspected rather than rerun under this review prohibition.
